sections.html:
Niles is a Cook County village on the far northwest edge of Chicago, with Skokie to the east, Morton Grove to the northeast, Glenview to the north and Park Ridge to the west. Population is 30,443 (July 1, 2025 estimate). The typical owner-occupied home is worth $358,700, and 74.6% of homes are owner-occupied. Much of the housing dates from the postwar building boom, when the village grew from 3,587 people in 1950 to 20,393 in 1960.

The village has its own transfer stamp with several steps that must be done before closing, so start early.

sections.h2: Transfer taxes at a Niles closing
sections.html:
Three transfer tax layers can apply to a Niles sale. The village rate is $3.00 per $1,000 of price, and the buyer pays it. The state and county rates come from the Cook County Clerk.

Transfer taxes on a Niles sale
LayerRateParty liable
State of Illinois.50 per $500Seller
Cook County.25 per $500Seller
Village of Niles$3.00 per $1,000, or fraction thereofBuyer

An exempt stamp, for a deed that is not a sale, costs a flat $25.00 and cannot be issued until all outstanding fines and fees are paid. For either stamp, the village requires a completed Niles Real Estate Transfer Declaration Form and a copy of the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration.

sections.h2: Before the transfer stamp is issued
sections.html:
Call the Finance Department at 847-588-8030 ten days before closing. The village uses that call to arrange a final water reading and a property search for fines, fees or violations.

The village will not issue a stamp unless the property is free of liens and violations and has no outstanding bills owed to the village. The practical points:

  • Buy stamps in person at the Finance Department in Niles Village Hall, or by mail to 1000 Civic Center Drive with a self-addressed, postage-paid envelope.
  • In-person transactions must reach the Finance Department before 4:30 pm with paperwork already complete.
  • Payment can be a cashier's check, money order, title company check, attorney firm check, cash, or a credit or debit card with a processing fee.
  • Completed forms can be emailed to the village's real estate transfer stamp address, with the property address in the subject line. Water reading and property search requests must be phoned in, not emailed.

A lien, an unpaid water bill or an open code violation will stop the stamp, so get the property search result early enough to fix anything that turns up.

If the transfer declarations show the new owner will not live there, the buyer must file a Rental License Application when buying the transfer stamp. Rental licenses are non-transferable when a property is sold, so the license you hold does not pass to the buyer.

That affects a landlord selling to another investor and a family selling a house that will be rented out. Questions about the application go to Community Development at 847-588-8040. If you have a tenant in place, check the lease and ask the buyer's side how it plans to apply for the license.

sections.h2: Transfer tax rebate for Niles residents who buy again
sections.html:
A narrow group qualifies. A Niles resident who sold a principal residence and buys a residential structure in the village to use as a principal residence can claim a rebate of $2 per $1,000, equal to two-thirds of the amount paid for the transfer stamp on the new property.

The buyer files after closing, with proof of the transaction, within one year of the sale of the old residence. The Finance Director reviews the claim, and commercial and retail property do not qualify. If you are moving up or down within Niles, keep the closing statements from both deals.

Several elementary districts cover the village: East Maine District 63, Park Ridge-Niles District 64, Golf District 67, Niles District 71 and Fairview District 72. High school students attend Maine Township District 207 or Niles Township Community District 219. Confirm the district for your address before you list.

Niles runs a free village bus, and Pace operates its Pulse Milwaukee and Pulse Dempster lines through town. U.S. 14 and Illinois routes 21, 43 and 58 cross the village, and Golf Mill Shopping Center is a long-standing retail anchor.

Median gross rent is $1,336. The village has 11,481 households averaging 2.51 people, and the median household income is $75,274. Of residents age 5 and older, 59.5% speak a language other than English at home, so listing materials in more than one language can reach more buyers.

Plan the Niles part of a sale around the stamp. First, sign the contract and agree on who pays each layer: the buyer pays the village stamp, and the seller is liable for the state and county charges. Second, call Finance ten days before closing for the water reading and property search. Third, clear any lien, unpaid bill or open violation the search finds, because the stamp waits on that.

Fourth, complete the Niles Real Estate Transfer Declaration Form along with the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, and get the paperwork to Village Hall before 4:30 pm if you are delivering it. Finally, if the buyer will rent the house out, make sure the Rental License Application goes in with the stamp request.

A cash buyer can often close on a short timeline, but the ten-day village call and the property search still apply, so build that lead time into any quick closing.

sections.h2: What to gather for the Niles stamp
sections.html:
Put a small folder together before you call Finance. It should hold the signed contract, the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, the completed Niles Real Estate Transfer Declaration Form, the property address and parcel number, and a payment method the village accepts. Title companies and attorneys often handle this step, so ask yours whether it will request the water reading and property search or whether you must phone them in yourself.

If the deed is not a sale, such as adding or removing a name, ask for the exempt stamp. It costs a flat $25.00, but the property still has to be clear of fines and fees first. Questions about open violations go to Community Development at 847-588-8040.

Finally, remember that email is fine for completed forms but not for the water reading or property search. Those need a phone call, and the ten-day clock starts when you make it.

faqs.q: Who pays the Niles real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer pays the village stamp, at $3.00 per $1,000 of price or fraction thereof. The state ($.50 per $500) and the county ($.25 per $500) are the seller's responsibility.

faqs.q: How early should I call the village before closing on a Niles house?
faqs.a: Ten days before closing. The Finance Department asks the seller to call 847-588-8030 so it can take a final water reading and run a property search for fines, fees and violations.

faqs.q: Can a Niles stamp be issued with an unpaid water bill or violation on the property?
faqs.a: No. The property must be free of liens and violations and cannot have outstanding bills owed to the village. Exempt stamps are also held until all fines and fees are paid.

faqs.q: What does a Niles buyer need if the house will be a rental?
faqs.a: A Rental License Application, filed at the time the transfer stamp is bought. Rental licenses do not carry over to the buyer when a property is sold.

faqs.q: Does Niles refund any of the transfer tax?
faqs.a: Only to a Niles resident who sold a principal residence and buys another residence in the village, and only on a form filed within one year. The rebate is $2 per $1,000, calculated as two-thirds of the stamp price paid on the new property.
